subject: Reserved GPU pricing, tenant isolation & SLOs — confirmation and next steps

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved GPU pricing, tenant isolation & SLOs — confirmation and next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for time earlier. Quick recap from our call plus the concrete next steps so everyone has alignment.

Summary of pain & goals (what you emphasized)
- Production latency spikes during peak 3-hour window (p95 ~ 1.2s today) causing customer-facing timeouts.
- Regulatory requirement: tenant isolation for PHI-sensitive models (separate GPU pools + audit logs).
- Need predictable monthly cost for Q1 budget review; team wants committed pricing vs on-demand.

What Redwood proposed on the call (high level)
1) Reserved GPU pool (dedicated) sized for steady-state inference: 6 x A100-equivalent instances (driver + 6 infer nodes) with burst policy to 9 nodes for 15% of traffic.
2) Tenant isolation option: dedicated VPC + isolated GPU pool, separate KMS scoping, and restricted operator role for your security team.
3) SLA targets: 99.9% uptime for reserved pool + latency SLOing guidance (p95 < 800ms under steady-state; automatic fallback to smaller model for sustained load).
4) Pricing: committed monthly fee + token-based overage. I outlined an initial estimate in the attached MOP and provided a simple SLA appendix.

Open items / decisions needed from MedicaHealth
- Procurement: approval of committed pool (6-node baseline / 9-node burst). Marcus, can procurement approve the baseline sizing and commit term (12 vs 24 months)?
- Security: sign-off on isolation design and KMS integration. Elena, can your security lead review the attached isolation diagram and reply with any gaps by EOD Friday?
- Acceptance criteria: confirm which latency tiers (p50/p95) you want included in the SLA; we recommended p95 < 800ms for the baseline workload.

Next steps (owners & ETA)
- Neha: Follow up with a tightened price proposal and ops runbook (deliverable: updated MOP) — ETA Wed 10/06.
- Aditya: Technical deep-dive on gRPC/kv-cache config and quantization tradeoffs if needed — propose a 45m session this week.
- Marcus / Procurement: confirm commitment term and PO cadence.

Attachments: MedicaHealth_Redwood_MOP_v1.pdf (ops + sizing), SLA-appendix-MedicaHealth.xlsx (SLO matrix + sample credits)

Appreciate the quick turn — happy to jump back on a call to walk through the MOP.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reserved GPU pricing, tenant isolation & SLOs — confirmation and next steps

Thanks Neha — good recap and much appreciated. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Sizing: the 6->9 baseline/burst seems reasonable. Two notes: we have a projected 25% growth for Nov due to a pilot expansion, so would like to lock a simple burst/baseline autoscale policy that doesn't require manual approvals.

2) Isolation: security wants explicit separation of logs (no aggregate telemetry that contains tokenized PHI). They also asked for an example audit log extract to validate that event-level entries are preserved. Can you include a sample audit snippet in the MOP?

3) SLA: procurement prefers a blended SLA: 99.8% availability for the first 3 months then bump to 99.9% after onboarding. Is that something Redwood can accept for a 12-month commitment?

Procurement note (Marcus): we'll need the committed pricing and a draft SOW/PO template to run through our internal buying process. Marcus, looping you to confirm timeline.

I'll review the attached MOP today and aim to get security feedback by Friday.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering | MedicaHealth

Elena — quick technical notes and what we'll include in the updated MOP:

- Autoscale policy: we can set a rule-based autoscaler (baseline 6 nodes, scale to 9 when sustained CPU or token throughput > 70% for 5 minutes) with a manual override flag for your ops team. If you want full hands-off, we can do an advanced policy that uses short-term forecasting (adds 1 node proactively when trend shows > 10% growth in 30 minutes).

- Audit logs: attaching a redacted example record in the MOP; logs include request_id, model_version, client_tenant_id, event_timestamp, latency_ms. No request payloads will be stored in plaintext for PHI-tagged routes per isolation mode.

- SLA ramp: the blended SLA approach is reasonable. For a 12-month commitment we can accept 99.8% for months 0-3 then 99.9% thereafter, with a clause that allows review after the pilot expansion in month 2. We'll put the exact credit schedule in the SLA appendix.

Action: I'll lead the MOP update and include both the audit snippet and an autoscale policy doc. Neha and I will have an internal review today and send the revised MOP by EOD 10/06.
